open_points.subject: deadline start instant
open_points.text: “the reading at the start plus the bound” does not define what event is “the start” for either caller
open_points.question: At what exact event must sandbox.execute_function and service_invoker.send_prepared_request take the initial monotonic reading from which the wall or transport deadline is derived?
options: Before any sandbox setup or process launch, and before any HTTP transport work including DNS and connection setup
Immediately after sandbox setup/process launch and immediately before the HTTP request begins transport work
A caller-specific boundary defined separately for the sandbox and HTTP transport
open_points.default_guess: Take one initial reading immediately before beginning all bounded work, including sandbox setup and all HTTP transport work.

open_points.subject: deadline expiration comparison
open_points.text: “asks whether it passed with a later reading” does not say whether equality means the deadline has passed
open_points.question: When a later monotonic reading equals the computed deadline exactly, is the bounded wait expired?

open_points.subject: deadline arithmetic
open_points.text: “the reading at the start plus the bound” does not fix the conversion and overflow semantics for adding the millisecond bound to a nanosecond reading
open_points.question: How must callers convert the millisecond bound to nanoseconds and handle an addition that exceeds the representation used for monotonic readings?
options: Use exact integer arithmetic and compare elapsed time without an overflowing absolute sum
Use checked multiplication and addition, with overflow producing an internal error
Use saturating arithmetic, clamping the deadline to the largest representable reading
open_points.default_guess: Use exact or widened integer arithmetic and compare elapsed nanoseconds against bound_ms × 1,000,000 without overflow.
